UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
DEPARTMENT OF THE TREASURY
FINANCIAL CRIMES ENFORCEMENT NETWORK
IN THE MATTER OF No. 2001 - 02
ANGELINA PLETT
ASSESSMENT OF CIVIL MONEY PENALTIES
AGAINST ANGELINA PLETT
I. INTRODUCTION
The Secretary of the United States Department of the Treasury has delegated to
the Director of the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (“FinCEN”) the authority to
determine whether a financial institution has violated the Bank Secrecy Act, 31 U.S.C.
§§5311 et seq. and 31 CFR Part 103 thereunder (“BSA”), and what, if any, sanction is
appropriate.
II. JURISDICTION
Angelina Plett (“Plett”) was, at all relevant times, an owner and the manager of
Cash For Checks Inc. (“Cash For Checks”). Cash For Checks was, at all relevant times, a
licensed check casher located in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma and was a “financial
institution” within the meaning of 31 U.S.C. §5312(a)(2) and 31 CFR §103.11(n).1
III. FINCEN’S DETERMINATIONS
A. Structuring
FinCEN has determined that between July 11, 1995, and April 26, 1996, Plett
willfully structured or willfully assisted in structuring check cashing transactions for
Joseph A. Sivigliano (“Sivigliano”) through a domestic financial institution in violation
of 31 U.S.C. §5324(a)(3) and 31 CFR §103.63(c). During the relevant time period,
Sivigliano cashed 136 checks totaling more than $1.17 million at Cash For Checks. On
each of 43 days, Sivigliano cashed a series of checks that individually totaled less than
$10,000, but that together exceeded $10,0

statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5324?
statutory.answer: Neutral — 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring to evade CTR reporting, but the facts do not show intent to evade or that the deposits were structured to avoid a required report.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 makes it unlawful to (i) structure or assist in structuring, or attempt to do so, (ii) for the purpose of evading the reporting requirements of 31 U.S.C. § 5313(a) (CTR reporting for currency transactions over $10,000), or (iii) cause/attempt to cause a domestic financial institution to fail to file a required report or file one with a material omission/misstatement. Here, the fact pattern shows seven cash deposits ranging from ~$5.5k to ~$8.8k labeled “sub-CTR cash deposit,” which is consistent with transactions below the $10,000 CTR threshold and could be consistent with structuring. However, § 5324 requires a purpose/intent to evade CTR reporting (not merely making multiple sub-$10k deposits). The facts do not state that any single day’s deposits aggregated above $10,000 at the same financial institution such that a CTR would have been required absent structuring, nor do they provide evidence of intent (e.g., statements about avoiding CTRs, instructions to split deposits, patterns tied to the $10k threshold at one bank, or evidence of causing a bank to not file a required CTR). Because the intent-to-evade element is not established on these facts, it cannot be determined that § 5324 applies. Contiguous phrase in answer and reasoning: “31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits”.
